summary: Self-service pod bootstrap: orchestrated Jira/Confluence/Slack provisioning with ownership handoff and audit trail
description:
Issue summary: Engineering pods currently request onboarding artifacts (Jira project, Confluence space, Slack channel, service account) via ad hoc tickets and manual work from platform ops. This request is to build a self-service pod-bootstrap webhook + approval flow that orchestrates creation and performs an ownership handoff with an auditable trail.

Background: We get repeated tickets to create new project sandboxes or feature pods. Manual provisioning is error-prone (permissions gaps, missing runbooks), and deprovisioning is inconsistent which bloats our tooling surfaces and increases audit risk. Several teams (model-eval, runtime-ops, infra-experiment) have similar requirements.

Impact: Reduces time-to-project by ~1-2 days, cuts repetitive work for platform SRE/ops, reduces stale channels/spaces, and improves compliance by centralizing audit records. This is internal but cross-org: improper permissioning could expose sensitive docs if not gated correctly.

Request details: Build an automated endpoint (pod-bootstrap webhook) that: 1) Accepts a minimal payload from a templated form (pod name, owner, privacy level, retention duration); 2) Creates a Jira project scaffolded from a template with default issue types and permission scheme; 3) Spins up a Confluence space using a runbook template and seeds a ‘Getting Started’ page with owners and links; 4) Provisions a Slack channel with naming conventions and auto-archival policy; 5) Creates scoped service account(s) and API tokens documented in the Confluence space; 6) Emits a signed audit record stored in our logs (and a Confluence audit page) and sends an acceptance message to the owners; 7) Enforces an approval gate (manager or platform-approver) before resources are created for elevated privacy levels.

Acceptance criteria: - A form can trigger the workflow and produce Jira/Confluence/Slack artifacts with correct naming/permissions. - Ownership is assigned in each system and visible in the generated runbook. - An auditable record (timestamp, requester, approver, artifact IDs) is produced and persisted. - Automatic archival and deprovisioning metadata is attached to each artifact. - Integration tests demonstrating successful end-to-end provisioning in staging exist.

Proposed flow (high level): 1) Developer opens 'Pod bootstrap' form (internal UI) -> 2) Workflow validates payload and checks policy -> 3) If required, sends approval request to manager/platform-approver -> 4) On approval, orchestrator calls Jira API (create project), Confluence API (create space + pages), Slack API (create channel + set retention), IAM API (create service account with least privilege) -> 5) Orchestrator writes audit record to centralized event store and posts link to generated runbook -> 6) Notification sent to owners.

Security & compliance notes: - Elevated pods (accessing customer data or private models) must require platform-approver and generate a KMS-wrapped service account secret stored in our secrets manager. - All tokens are time-boxed and rotated automatically. - All created artifacts get a data-classification label that surface in Confluence and Jira.

Dependencies: - Slack provisioning API quota and a service bot token with channel creation scope. - Jira project creation API and a platform permission scheme. - Confluence template that exists or will be created by Content team. - RBAC review from Security for the approval matrix.

Rollout plan: Prototype in staging (two pilot pods) -> security review -> soft-launch for a single org (model-eval) -> refine based on feedback -> GA to all pods.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - this is a provisioning automation request. Existing manual repro: file ticket, wait 24-72h for ops, verify artifacts and request missing permissions.
investigation_notes: Spoke with pod leads in model-eval and runtime-ops. They want a single-button pathway to create consistent runbooks and channels. Platform ops estimates ~24 engineer-hours for a minimal prototype (orchestrator + templates + tests). Need to confirm Slack app token scope and whether channel auto-archive is available via API in all workspaces. Jira Cloud allows project creation via API under our admin token but requires permission scheme template creation. Confluence templates can be created programmatically but content team wants a draft template first.
